Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to help you settle into motherhood and to make sure you’re getting the support you need.  

Today we’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. It’s simply ten questions about how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days. Your answers are completely confidential and will help us figure out the best next steps for your emotional health. There are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you right now.

Whenever you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question.
Hi, Dr. Martinez. Okay… I’m ready when you are.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Mostly… no, not really. I’ll smile if something’s genuinely funny, but it feels kind of forced and the laugh fades fast. Nothing feels as amusing as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Sometimes, but it’s pretty rare. Every now and then I’ll think, “That might be nice,” but the excitement never really kicks in the way it did before the baby. Mostly everything just feels flat.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… quite a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I keep thinking it must be something I did—like I’m not doing the “mom thing” right. Even little stuff, like spitting up more than usual, makes me feel I’ve messed up somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, that happens most days. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly wonder if she’s breathing okay, or I’ll lie down and picture the stroller tipping even though it’s locked. There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just keep looping and I can’t switch them off for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Out of nowhere my heart starts racing and I feel like something awful is about to happen, even when I’m just sitting on the couch. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most of the time. I can still get through the feedings and diaper changes, but it feels like I’m barely treading water. When she won’t nap or I can’t finish a single chore, it piles up and I just want to sit on the floor and cry.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Uh-huh. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby, and I can’t drift off. Even when I do sleep, I jerk awake at least once or twice a night with my heart pounding and the anxious thoughts right there.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… pretty much every day. I wouldn’t say it’s all-day tears, but there’s this heavy, gray cloud feeling that just hangs over everything. Even when I’m holding her and she’s calm, I still feel down, like I’m missing the joy everyone keeps telling me I should feel.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, once or twice this week. It’s usually when everything piles up—she won’t sleep, the house is a mess, and I feel like I’m failing. I’ll just start crying while rocking her, trying to stay quiet so she doesn’t get upset too.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…Yeah. It’s popped into my head once or twice—just a quick, scary flash of “what if I weren’t here,” but I shake it off right away. I don’t want to die; I just want the pressure and sadness to stop. I haven’t made any plans or anything like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary**  
*Patient*: Postpartum mother (infant age not specified)  
*Date*: [today]

### 1. Positive Screening Indicators (EPDS ≥ probable clinical range)
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia (Q1, Q2, Q8)
- Daily tearfulness, feeling "heavy/gray" (Q8, Q9)
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)
- Anxious preoccupations & panic episodes without clear trigger (Q4, Q5)
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed, "treading water" (Q6)
- Initial insomnia and nighttime arousals associated with racing thoughts (Q7)

### 2. Safety Flag
- Passive suicidal ideation (Q10): fleeting thoughts "what if I weren’t here," no plan or intent reported; patient immediately dismisses thoughts

### 3. Functional Impact
- Feeding/care tasks completed, but reports "barely coping," frequent crying spells, and impaired nocturnal sleep

### 4. Screening Impression
Responses indicate high likelihood of major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety in the postpartum period; passive SI present → requires immediate risk assessment and referral for psychiatric evaluation.

### 5. Recommended Next Steps (for documenting team)
- Administer standardized EPDS scoring; consider PHQ-9/GAD-7
- Arrange same-week follow-up (OB, psychiatry, or behavioral health)
- Provide crisis resources; develop safety plan
- Coordinate support services (e.g., home health, peer support)

*End of screening note*
